subject: Post-call: Pathfinder AI — scope, pain points & procurement next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@pathfinder.ai>
Cc: Tom Raines <tom.raines@pathfinder.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery

Hi Claire / Tom — thanks again for your time today. Wanted to summarize the key points we heard and propose a concise next-step plan so we stay aligned.

TL;DR — Primary pains: latency spikes on batch scoring, unpredictable cost at peak traffic, and audit requirements for data lineage. Success criteria: 99th pct latency below 300ms for user-facing calls, monthly inference cost reduction of ~25% on peak windows, and auditable request logs retained for 12 months.

What we heard (high level):
- Current stack: Pathfinder runs a mixture of open Llama-family models and a proprietary fine-tune on GCP (pre-emptible + autoscaling groups). Inference happens through an in-house microservice with limited KV caching; they use a custom batching layer that often causes latency tail issues.
- Pain: tail latency during bursts (notable during business hours), costs spike due to many small sequential requests, and compliance wants clearer audit logs and KMS integration for keys.
- Constraints: team wants to avoid full rewrite; preference for a controlled pilot on a subset of models/traffic; security requires vendor SOC2 Type II evidence and a short checklist for KMS and VPC options.

Commercial/Procurement signals:
- Decision timeline: target decision by end of Q2 (internal exec sync on 6/20).
- Stakeholders: Engineering lead (Tom), Head of ML Ops (Claire), Procurement (Emily Park, TBD), Security (CISO office).
- Initial guardrails: pilot scope should be 2-3 models, up to 16k tokens/day, and a max committed throughput (p50) of ~500 rps during the pilot window. They prefer not to sign a long-term annual commitment without an initial proof point.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) I will send a short commercial framing doc with pilot guardrails + estimated pricing bands for the pilot. (Action: Vivek, by Tue 5/12)
2) Pathfinder to share a short risk matrix + list of compliance questions and their procurement timeline. (Action: Claire, by Fri 5/15)
3) Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Marcus (serving/runtime) and Tom to validate integration path for prefix caching and KMS. (Action: Monica to coordinate, target week of 5/18)
4) If all good, we prepare a 30-day pilot SOW and an SLA summary for their security and procurement teams.

Attachments: I'll attach a short Redwood SLA summary and an example risk matrix template for you to populate.

Thanks again — I think there's a clear path for a low-risk pilot that answers the latency/cost questions quickly.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0167

---
Attachment stubs: redwood-sla-summary.pdf (3 pages), pathfinder-risk-matrix.xlsx (1 sheet)

From: Claire Huang <claire@pathfinder.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Raines <tom.raines@pathfinder.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery

Thanks Vivek — helpful recap. Confirming a few details and adding clarifications from our side.

A few clarifications:
- The "latency spikes" are most obvious for our conversational API under heavy short-session traffic; the 99th spikes to ~900ms during peak minutes (we measured this last week). P50 is usually ~80-120ms.
- We have a short list of compliance asks: SOC2 evidence (we need the report or a vendor summary), KMS/HSM integration options, and the ability to host logs for 12 months in our AWS account.
- Procurement: Emily Park will own the process; I can introduce you next week. They typically run a 30-45 day review for pilots.

Agree with the 4-step next-step plan. Two small asks for your pilot framing doc: please include an explicit rollback and data-retention clause for the pilot, and outline what fallback behavior looks like if latency targets aren’t met.

I attached a very rough risk matrix (see pathfinder-risk-matrix.xlsx) with a few items already noted. We'll fill out more after the security sync.

Appreciate the fast follow-up — I look forward to the tech deep-dive with Marcus.

Best,
Claire Huang
Head of ML Ops | Pathfinder AI
claire@pathfinder.ai

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery — pilot framing attached

Claire / Tom — appreciate the quick confirmation. I attached a short commercial framing PDF (redwood-sla-summary.pdf) and populated the pilot guardrails inside the risk matrix template you uploaded. Key commercial notes below for visibility and so procurement has a starting point:

Commercial framing (pilot):
- Scope: 2 models (one conversational, one reranker), limited to 16k tokens/day and up to 500 rps peak for pilot windows. Pilot duration: 30 days.
- Pricing: two-tier band — measured usage token pricing for the pilot (pay-as-you-go) + a modest reserved burst block for guaranteed throughput during peak minutes. Provided estimated ranges in the attached PDF.
- SLA & rollback: Red/Amber/Green latency thresholds defined in the SLA. If 99th percentile latency exceeds 600ms for two consecutive days we trigger a joint incident and we have a predefined rollback to their current microservice.
- Security: we will provide SOC2 summary docs and a short KMS integration playbook. Logs can be exported to Pathfinder's AWS account for retention; we'll draft the config in the tech deep-dive.

Next steps (updated):
- Vivek: deliver finalized pricing bands + populated risk matrix. (By Tue 5/12)
- Monica: set up tech deep-dive with Marcus and Tom (Target: 5/19 11:00 PT).
- Claire: intro to Emily Park (Procurement) — once intro done, I'll drop an SOW template and an initial DocuSign option.
- Lauren: I'm looping you for visibility on commercial guardrails and to help expedite procurement if needed.

If that looks correct I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the 5/19 deep-dive.

Thanks — Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
